Abhorrent

ab-HOR-ent · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Abhorrent is inspiring disgust and loathing.

Testing cosmetics on animals struck her as abhorrent, and she refused to buy from any brand that still did it.

Worked Example

The documentary exposed conditions at the factory that were truly abhorrent -- workers locked in overnight, no safety equipment, wages withheld for months at a time.

Abhorrent describes something that inspires deep disgust and moral revulsion -- the conditions aren't just bad, they're shocking and repellent.

How Abhorrent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

revolting

revolting: causing intense dislike or disgust

loathsome

loathsome: extremely unpleasant; hateful

Antonyms

admirable

admirable: deserving respect and approval

delightful

delightful: causing delight; charming

How Strong Is It? — unpleasant → abhorrent → monstrous

unpleasant vs. abhorrent

unpleasant vs. abhorrent: Unpleasant describes something mildly disagreeable, far short of true disgust.

monstrous vs. abhorrent

monstrous vs. abhorrent: Monstrous describes something so extreme and shocking that it goes beyond even abhorrent -- almost beyond belief.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — ab-

prefix — ab-: away from (Latin)

root — horr-

root — horr-: to bristle, to shudder with dread (Latin horrere)

suffix — -ent

suffix — -ent: being in a state of (adjective-forming) (Latin -ens)

Put it together

Put it together: Abhorrent comes from Latin ab- ('away from') + horrere ('to shudder with dread') -- literally describing something that makes you shudder and pull away.

Use the root in a new word: horror

Use the root in a new word: horror: The audience sat in stunned horror as the plot twist was revealed.

Root Check

Word Choice

Abhorrent describes the repulsive quality of a thing or an act -- a policy, a crime, a condition -- rather than a person's feeling about it. It shares its Latin root (horrere, 'to shudder with dread') with abhor, a verb taught elsewhere in this course; abhorrent describes what abhor is a reaction to.
